text: What is the correct status of the halting problem HALT = {⟨P,x⟩ : P halts on x}?
choices: It is decidable, but only in exponential time
It is undecidable: no algorithm decides it for all inputs
It is decidable for Turing machines but not for real computers
It is an open problem whether it is decidable
explanation: Turing (1936) proved HALT is undecidable — no algorithm correctly answers 'does P halt on x?' for all P and x. It is not merely 'hard' (A) nor open (D); undecidability is a proven impossibility, not a complexity bound. By the Church–Turing thesis this applies to any model of computation, including real computers (contra C).
